settings.name: pgaudit.log_client
settings.description: Specifies whether audit messages should be visible to the client. This setting should generally be left disabled but may be useful for debugging or other purposes.

settings.name: pgaudit.log_level
settings.description: Specifies the log level that will be used for log entries. This setting is used for regression testing and may also be useful to end users for testing or other purposes.  It is not intended to be used in a production environment as it may leak which statements are being logged to the user.

settings.name: pgaudit.log_parameter
settings.description: Specifies that audit logging should include the parameters that were passed with the statement. When parameters are present they will be be included in CSV format after the statement text.

settings.name: pgaudit.log_parameter_max_size
settings.description: Specifies, in bytes, the maximum length of variable-length parameters to log.  If 0 (the default), parameters are not checked for size.  If set, when the size of the parameter is longer than the setting, the value in the audit log is replaced with a placeholder. Note that for character types, the length is in bytes for the parameter's encoding, not characters.

settings.name: pgaudit.log_relation
settings.description: Specifies whether session audit logging should create a separate log entry for each relation referenced in a SELECT or DML statement. This is a useful shortcut for exhaustive logging without using object audit logging.

settings.name: pgaudit.log_rows
settings.description: Specifies whether logging will include the rows retrieved or affected by a statement.

settings.name: pgaudit.log_statement
settings.description: Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters.  Depending on requirements, the full statement text might not be required in the audit log.

settings.name: pgaudit.log_statement_once
settings.description: Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters with the first log entry for a statement/substatement combination or with every entry.  Enabling this setting will result in less verbose logging but may make it more difficult to determine the statement that generated a log entry, though the statement/substatement pair along with the process id should suffice to identify the statement text logged with a previous entry.

settings.name: pgaudit.role
